deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): K^1 is a 1-complex 'subdivided into pseudo-lines'. Every vertex lies on at least two pseudo-lines, and any two distinct pseudo-lines meet in exactly one point. This is a purely combinatorial axiomatisation of the 1-skeleton of an arrangement of pseudolines in the real projective plane. For each pseudo-line D, Ω(D) is the 2-element set of orientations of D. For a vertex s on neither D nor D' there is a bijection φ_{s;D,D'}: Ω(D) ≅ Ω(D'), geometrically 'perspective from s', subject to axioms a), b), c). Axiom b) says φ_{s;D,D'} depends only on which of the two arcs of a third pseudo-line Δ, cut out by Δ∩D and Δ∩D', contains s.

This page does three things.
(1) It ends a discussion of uniqueness. If the system admits automorphisms of a certain kind, the system of isomorphisms is invariant under them, so it is not unique. This happens when there is a bigon, and a fortiori a monogon. A monogon means a pencil: all pseudo-lines through one point. A bigon means a 'double pencil': a pencil together with the pseudo-line joining the two foci. These are the degenerate configurations.
(2) Assume there is neither monogon nor bigon. For each vertex s, define Ω(s) as the quotient of the disjoint union of the Ω(D), over pseudo-lines D not through s, by the identifications φ_{s;D,D'}. It is a 2-element set. Topologically, Ω(D) ≅ Ω(s) is the classical fact that the complement of D in RP^2 is a disc. An orientation of that disc at s induces, via the degree-2 boundary map, an orientation of D. So Ω(s) is the set of local orientations of the plane at s.
(3) Make s ↦ Ω(s) a local system on K^1. For an edge I with ends s, s', the hypotheses supply a pseudo-line D through neither s nor s'. Define Ω(s) ≅ Ω(D) ≅ Ω(s'). Independence of D follows from b). Take another such D'. The edge I lies on some pseudo-line Δ and contains no vertex other than its ends, so Δ∩D and Δ∩D' are not interior to I. Hence s and s' lie on the same arc, and φ_{s;D,D'} = φ_{s';D,D'}. The next page notes this independence is in fact equivalent to b).

The resulting local system is the combinatorial orientation sheaf of RP^2. Its monodromy is nontrivial along cycles that run once along a pseudo-line. The overall programme, continued on the next page, is to reconstruct the 'carte' (the cellular map of RP^2) from the combinatorial K^1 alone. The remaining steps are a cyclic ('polygonal') structure on the edges at each vertex (a rotation system), and a canonical bijection between Ω(s) and one of its two orientations.
errors: The independence argument tacitly assumes that an edge of K^1 lies on a single pseudo-line and has no interior vertices. That is implicit in 'complexe subdivisé en ps. droites', but it is not stated.
Existence of a pseudo-line avoiding both ends of an edge is invoked 'par hyp.'. It needs the no-monogon/no-bigon hypothesis or some genericity, and it is not explicitly justified on the page.

The claim that Ω(s) has exactly two elements requires that the φ_{s;D,D'} be coherent (cocycle condition φ_{D',D''}∘φ_{D,D'} = φ_{D,D''}). Presumably this is meant to follow from a)–c), but it is not checked here.

ideas.what: Axiomatic combinatorial characterisation of the 1-skeleton of a pseudoline arrangement (any two pseudo-lines meet exactly once), with perspectivity bijections between orientation sets
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial/axiomatic pseudoline arrangements; cf. allowable sequences, local sequences, oriented matroids of rank 3
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's published texts to my knowledge; the 'cartes' theme appears in Esquisse d'un programme, but not pseudoline axiomatics

ideas.what: Ω(s) defined as a colimit of orientation sets Ω(D) over pseudo-lines avoiding s, then glued into a local system on K^1
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial orientation double cover / orientation local system of RP^2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical topology (orientation sheaf); combinatorial version folklore

ideas.what: Non-uniqueness exactly in the pencil (monogon) and double-pencil (bigon) cases
ideas.modern_name: Degenerate (near-pencil) arrangements; uniqueness of embedding failing for low face-width
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; cf. uniqueness-of-embedding results of Whitney (planar) and Robertson–Vitray / Mohar (projective plane)

ideas.what: Reconstructing the map (rotation system plus orientation data) from the abstract 1-skeleton
ideas.modern_name: Graph determines embedding / rigidity of projective-planar embeddings

missed.claim: A programme to reconstruct the full cellular map of RP^2 from purely incidence-combinatorial axioms on the 1-skeleton of a pseudoline arrangement. It proceeds by first building the orientation local system from perspectivity bijections, then a rotation system. The programme is left incomplete (next page: 'il faudrait encore définir une structure polygonale...').
missed.quote: On peut maintenant, dans les cas où il n'y a ni monogône ni bigône, définir pour tout sommet s Ω(s) comme l'ens. quotient ... C'est un ens. à deux éléments, ... il faut en faire un syst. local sur K^1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives a perspectivity-based, sheaf-like derivation of the orientation character of RP^2 from abstract pseudoline incidence data. It complements the oriented-matroid and graph-embedding uniqueness literature. It is a modest but distinctive viewpoint linking Grothendieck's 'cartes' to discrete geometry.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful and correct, but essentially an elementary combinatorial reconstruction of a classical object (the orientation sheaf of RP^2). The uniqueness-of-embedding phenomena are known in topological graph theory. The novelty lies mainly in the framing and in Grothendieck's interest in pseudoline arrangements.
transcription_corrections: 'une bigône C par une plus haut [?] sur [?] qu'il y a une mono-gone' is probably '(à plus forte raison s'il y a un monogône, i.e. s'il s'agit d'un faisceau de ps.-dr.)'; there is an opening parenthesis matched later.
'contenant [-...-] ps.-droite qui joint les deux foyers' reads as 'double faisceau con[tenant la] ps.-droite qui joint les deux foyers'.
'et par [?] on définit' should read 'et par D on définit Ω(s) ≅ Ω(s') comme le composé', with diagram Ω(s) → Ω(D) → Ω(s').
'l'ens. quotient de l'ens. des Ω(D)' means the quotient of the union (disjoint sum) of the Ω(D).
